'''Eric Jakeman''' (born 1939) is a British [[mathematical physics|mathematical physicist]] specialising in the [[statistics]] and [[quantum statistics]] of [[wave]]s. He is an emeritus professor at the [[University of Nottingham]].

== Education ==
Jakeman was educated at [[The Brunts School]] in  [[Mansfield]], England.<ref name="whoswho" />  He received a degree in mathematical physics from [[Birmingham University]] in 1960, and a PhD in [[superconductivity]] theory in 1963.<ref name="Jakeman 2006" />

== Career ==
He was the head of the scattering and [[quantum optics]] section at the [[Defence Research Agency]], a visiting professor at [[Imperial College London]], an honorary secretary of the [[Institute of Physics]] from 1994 until 2003, and finally a Professor of Applied Statistical Optics at the [[University of Nottingham]] from 1996. He was a member of the Council of the [[European Physical Society]] from 1985 until 2003.<ref name="whoswho" /><ref name="IOP1994" /><ref name="Jakeman 2006" />

== Awards and honours ==
In 1977, Jakeman received the [[Maxwell Medal and Prize|Maxwell Medal]] of the Institute of Physics for his work on [[statistical optics]].<ref name="IOP1994" /><ref name="Physics" /> He was elected a [[List of Fellows of the Royal Society elected in 1990|Fellow of the Royal Society (FRS) in 1990]].<ref name="FRS">{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/eric-jakeman-11694|title=Eric Jakeman|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London}} One or more of the preceding sentences may incorporate text from the royalsociety.org website where "all text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]."</ref> His certificate of election reads: {{centered pull quote|Dr Jakeman is an internationally recognised expert in the statistics and quantum statistics of wave fields, particularly those arising in [[laser]] [[scattering]].  His theoretical work on [[photon statistics]] and [[speckle pattern|speckle]] has made a unique contribution to the development of the technique of [[photon correlation spectroscopy]] which is now used to investigate structure and motion in a wide range of systems of importance in engineering, medicine, physics, chemistry and biology.  He has also significantly advanced the subject of [[Non-Gaussianity|non-Gaussian]] scattering of waves by random media and has developed new [[noise]] models which are being widely applied in optical, microwave and acoustic scattering problems.

Jakeman has also made contributions to the field of [[heat transfer|heat]] and [[mass transfer]], particularly on the subjects of morphological stability and oscillatory [[convection]] in [[crystal growth]], and was jointly responsible for the notion of [[Double diffusive convection|doubly-diffusive convection]] driven by the [[Soret effect|Soret Effect]].<ref name="frsCitation">{{cite web|url=https://collections.royalsociety.org/DServe.exe?dsqIni=Dserve.ini&dsqApp=Archive&dsqCmd=Show.tcl&dsqDb=Catalog&dsqPos=0&dsqSearch=%28RefNo%3D%27EC%2F1990%2F17%27%29|title=EC/1990/17: Jakeman, Eric|publisher=[[The Royal Society]]|access-date=6 July 2017}}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>}}
